chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch.340: Zhuge Yuan Appears & Facai Dies in a Hall of Mirrors
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang meets the mysterious scholar Zhuge Yuan, who heals him and warns of a Knife-Pawnbroker’s curse. An identity crisis erupts with three pairs of doppelgangers, and the Chief Recorder reveals that Facai of the Three Yuan is already dead.
og_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch.340 — Making a Fortune
og_description: A scholar who can see through invisibility, a hall of identical impostors, and a shrunken head that spells doom. The lies pile up.
twitter_title: DGYX 340: Who’s the Real Li Huowang? (Spoiler: Nobody Knows)
twitter_description: Zhuge Yuan makes his debut, heals Li Huowang, and leaves a mysterious spindle. But with two Li Huowangs, two Hong Das, and two Heart-Bewilderments, trust is a joke. Plus: Facai is dead.

lore_anchors.definition: A mysterious scholar who appears at the Bone Buddha Temple. His fan bears the inscription “Tian Sheng Wo Cai” (Heaven Gave Me Talent). He can see through invisibility, detect anomalies in the Five Phases, and offers genuine kindness—though Li Huowang suspects he is a Zuowandao.

A folkloric figure who loans blades and later collects the borrower’s luck or fortune as repayment. The rusty knives stuck in Li Huowang’s face belong to one such pawnbroker, carrying a metaphysical lien on his destiny.
A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office. He carries a gold abacus and holds significant bureaucratic and supernatural authority.
An elusive trio within the Supervisory Heavenly Office: Facai (Making a Fortune), Kuaile (Happiness), and Ping’an (Safety). Facai’s death signals a threat far beyond the current squabble.
A mysterious object left behind by Zhuge Yuan. Li Huowang dismisses it but later its value becomes clear.
A monk with the “Mind-Penetration” ability that allows him to discern truth from falsehood—but when two identical Heart-Bewilderment monks appear, the ability becomes useless.
Li Huowang’s alias within the Supervisory Heavenly Office, given to him to conceal his true identity.
